---
title: Attach a schema to a dataset
description: Declare column types, units, and constraints so downstream tasks can validate
---

A `Dataset` or `Table` without a schema is opaque: a reader of the diagram cannot tell what columns exist or what they contain. Attaching a schema closes that gap and lets tooling validate that upstream tasks produce, and downstream tasks consume, compatible data.

## Two ways to attach a schema

A `Dataset` or a `Table` carries a `schema` attribute that points at a `Schema` element; the `Schema` element carries a `format` (`csvw`, `linkml`, `jsonschema`, ...) and a `body`.

**Inline.** Put the schema text itself in the `Schema` element's `body`. The schema is part of the diagram and travels with the `.studyflow` file. Use this for small datasets where the schema is short and study-specific.

**By reference.** Put a path or URL to an external schema file in the `body` instead. Use this when the schema is shared across studies (e.g., BIDS, Psych-DS, a CSVW URL).

Both forms render the same way in the modeler; the difference is whether the schema text lives inside or outside the `.studyflow` file.

## CSVW for tabular data

For tabular data, [CSV on the Web (CSVW)](https://w3c.github.io/csvw/) is the recommended schema format. A minimal CSVW schema looks like this:

```json
{
  "@context": "http://www.w3.org/ns/csvw",
  "url": "trials.csv",
  "tableSchema": {
    "columns": [
      { "name": "participantId", "datatype": "string", "required": true },
      { "name": "trialIndex", "datatype": "integer", "minimum": 0 },
      { "name": "condition", "datatype": "string", "valueUrl": "#congruent|#incongruent" },
      { "name": "rt", "datatype": "number", "minimum": 0 },
      { "name": "correct", "datatype": "boolean" }
    ]
  }
}
```

Reference it from your `Table` element by setting its `schema` to a `Schema` element with `format: csvw` and the URL or relative path of the CSVW file as its `body`.

## Standard schemas

For domain-specific data, prefer a community standard over a hand-rolled schema:

- **[BIDS](https://bids.neuroimaging.io/)** -- Brain Imaging Data Structure, for neuroimaging.
- **[Psych-DS](https://psych-ds.github.io/)** -- psychology dataset standard for behavioral data.
- **Behaverse [Events](https://behaverse.org/data-model/spec/events/index.html) and [Trials](https://behaverse.org/data-model/spec/trials/index.html)** -- Behaverse data models for behavioral experiments.

The element catalog has icons for each of these -- see [Elements](../reference/elements.qmd). Point the dataset's `schema` at a `Schema` element whose `body` is the standard's URL.

## Schemas on non-tabular data

For arrays (tensors, images, fMRI volumes, video), use a `Dataset` instead of a `Table` and set a schema that documents dimensions, dtype, and units. For neuroimaging, BIDS is usually sufficient and you can reference its sidecar `.json` files directly.

## What schemas enable

Once a dataset has a schema:

- **The modeler validates** that data-operation tasks (`Map`, `Filter`) reference columns the schema declares.
- **The runtime can refuse** to write data that violates the schema, catching bugs at production time rather than analysis time.
- **Downstream tasks read confidently** -- a `Reduce` over a column knows the column's type.
- **Reviewers see the data contract** without reading code.

## Checklist

- [ ] Every `Dataset` and `Table` has a `schema`.
- [ ] Column names in the schema match the names used by upstream tasks.
- [ ] Units and constraints are present where they matter (RT minimum, accuracy in [0, 1], etc.).
- [ ] External schema URLs are stable (don't reference a moving target).
